solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Slave-driver teacher after a job

indicators.note: after places the teacher's word behind the job's word

parts.note: a job to be done is a task
a schoolmaster is a teacher, so master will do

explanation.surface: A harsh teacher is chasing after some work.
explanation.definitionFit: A demanding overseer who works people hard is a slave-driver, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: People go crazy running it

parts.note: the idiom is to 'run' this word when one behaves wildly, so the clue describes the phrase it completes

explanation.surface: A description of people losing their heads while running something.
explanation.definitionFit: To run wild in a frenzy is the fixed idiom built on this Malay-derived word for frenzy.

clue.text: A thousand odd times is a lot

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for a thousand (kilo)

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of times are strangely arranged

explanation.surface: A thousand odd occasions add up to a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' turns TIMES into ISMET. 'A lot' looks like 'a great deal', but lot here means one's fate.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot is one's destiny or fate, which is the meaning of this word borrowed from Arabic via Turkish.

clue.text: Accepts birds are raised on board a ship

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting between its letters SS

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Someone takes it as given that birds are being reared aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'are raised' reads the birds upwards; 'on board' a ship is the crossword convention for going inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume something is to accept it as true without proof, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Travel after star of film and TV

definitions.meaning: a long arduous journey on foot is this

definitions.text: after star of film and TV
definitions.meaning: the word that follows Star in the title of the science-fiction TV series and films

explanation.surface: A celebrity of screen and television goes on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, hard journey, so it is a synonym for travel; Star Trek is the famous franchise.

clue.text: Go back to the nunnery

definitions.meaning: a secluded religious house where one withdraws from the world

explanation.surface: Someone decides to return to the convent.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw, and a retreat is also a quiet religious refuge such as a convent.

clue.text: Charles I wandering round an English county

indicators.note: round means the scrambled king's letters wrap around the word an
wandering suggests the letters of Charles I stray into a new order

explanation.surface: King Charles the First roams around a county of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an English county' tempts you to take 'an' as part of the definition, but it is the piece the scrambled king's letters go 'round'; 'wandering' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a county in north-west England, its county town being Lancaster.

clue.text: Cowardly character shown up by a referee?

parts.note: yellow is slang for cowardly
a card is an eccentric character

explanation.surface: A timid person is exposed by an umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown up' means literally held up: in football the referee raises this as a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: Football referees hold up this coloured card to caution a player, so it is literally shown up.

clue.text: Husband consumed with enmity

parts.note: consumed food means ate it

explanation.surface: A husband is eaten up with hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity and hatred are both deep hostility, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Sticking to principles, agree to include its reform

indicators.note: to include means the first word takes the other inside it

parts.note: to agree is to consent

indicators.note: reform means the letters of its are formed anew

explanation.surface: Someone holding fast to their principles agrees to include its reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' turns ITS into IST, which CONSENT is made 'to include'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sticking to principles acts in the same way each time, which is being steady and unchanging.

clue.text: Car's crashed by a learner — a culpable character

indicators.note: crashed suggests a wreck, so the letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: the 's supplies an S here
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A car is crashed by a learner driver, who is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' turns CARSAL into the answer; here 'Car's' gives CARS, its apostrophe-S counting as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous or dishonest person, someone guilty of misdeeds, so a culpable character.

clue.text: Chessmen in defensive situations

definitions.meaning: rooks, the chess pieces shaped like towers

explanation.surface: Chess pieces placed in defensive positions.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks are informally called castles, and castles are fortified buildings for defence.

clue.text: Issue raised by a gold prospector

definitions.text: Issue raised by a gold prospector

parts.words: Issue raised by a gold prospector
parts.note: issue means offspring: the old song tells of a miner, a forty-niner, and his daughter

explanation.surface: A gold prospector raises a point of contention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue raised' reads as a matter brought up, but it is a child brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: In the folk song 'Oh My Darling', this girl is the daughter of a miner in the California gold rush.

clue.text: Train officer, one of the same class

parts.note: to train someone is to school them
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A railway train officer is in the same class as someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow pupil at the same school, in the same class, is this.

clue.text: A bit quiet and embarrassed

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
embarrassed people turn red

explanation.surface: Someone is a little quiet and embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shred is a small scrap or fragment, so a bit, as in 'not a shred of evidence'.

clue.text: Orchestra was taken aback by a wood instrument

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, like an orchestra

indicators.note: taken aback here means the word was is taken backwards

explanation.surface: An orchestra was startled by a woodwind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns WAS into SAW. 'Wood instrument' suggests woodwind, but it is a tool for cutting wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandsaw is a power tool with an endless toothed band for cutting wood.

clue.text: Feel depressed and inferior?

definitions.meaning: to ... in spirits, split as two words

explanation.surface: Someone feels down and second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as 'be low' it means feel depressed; as one word it means lower or beneath, so inferior.

clue.text: Such music is not bound to sell

definitions.text: Such music is not bound to sell

parts.words: Such music is not bound to sell
parts.note: printed music sold as loose pages rather than a bound book; 'not bound to sell' reads as unlikely to sell

explanation.surface: This kind of music is not guaranteed to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheet music is printed on unbound loose pages and sold that way.

clue.text: She was spurned by Narcissus, it's recalled

definitions.meaning: the nymph in Greek myth who loved Narcissus and was rejected
a sound that is called back, repeated by reflection

explanation.surface: A woman rejected by Narcissus is remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: The nymph rejected by Narcissus faded to just a voice, and a reflected sound repeats or recalls a call.

clue.text: Very keen to make a comeback as a singer

indicators.note: making a comeback means the word comes back, read backwards

parts.note: avid means very keen

explanation.surface: A very eager performer attempts a return to the stage as a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: A short release from the army

definitions.text: A short release from the army

parts.words: A short release from the army
parts.note: the word is a shortening of the term for discharge from military service

explanation.surface: A brief leave from army service.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob is the abbreviated form of demobilisation, the release of troops from service.

clue.text: A sound measure

parts.note: reads as a sensible step, but means a unit for measuring loudness

explanation.surface: A sensible step to take.
explanation.definitionFit: This logarithmic unit measures sound intensity, so it is literally a measure of sound.

clue.text: Will live on an exploratory expedition

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the first word on top of the second

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a quest is a search or expedition

explanation.surface: A man will live on an expedition of exploration.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest is a legacy left by will, so the noun stands for what a will gives.

clue.text: Having developed, went round topless

indicators.note: topless means the word's first letter is removed

parts.note: went round means revolved

explanation.surface: Someone who has matured went round without a top on.
explanation.definitionFit: Evolved means having developed gradually, so the past forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Chap comes in to work in the garden for a few days

indicators.note: comes in means the chap's name goes inside the gardening word

parts.note: to weed is to clear a garden of weeds
Ken is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A man comes round to do some gardening for a few days.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekend is Saturday and Sunday, a short break of a few days.

clue.text: Skiers may provide one with an oral greeting

indicators.note: may provide suggests the letters of skiers can be rearranged to supply something else

explanation.surface: Skiers may offer someone a spoken welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral greeting' sounds like a spoken hello, but it is a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: One who kisses greets with the mouth, so with an oral greeting; it is also slang for the mouth.

clue.text: Visible remains of an ancient undertaking

definitions.text: Visible remains of an ancient undertaking

parts.words: Visible remains of an ancient undertaking
parts.note: undertaking reads as a project, but means burial by an undertaker; the remains are earth mounds over graves

explanation.surface: Traces of a long-ago project still visible today.
explanation.definitionFit: These are prehistoric burial mounds, visible earthworks marking ancient graves.

clue.text: Boast about dress

indicators.note: about means the word is turned around, read backwards

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress

explanation.surface: Someone shows off about their dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To boast and to brag both mean to talk proudly of oneself.

clue.text: List of biblical books held by academy

indicators.note: held by means the books sit inside the academy's letters

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy
OT is the Old Testament, a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: A catalogue of Bible books is kept by an academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a list of people and their turns of duty.

clue.text: Suitable music for the hairdressers' ball?

definitions.text: Suitable music for the hairdressers' ball?

parts.words: Suitable music for the hairdressers' ball?
parts.note: a dance for hair-cutters would fittingly have close-harmony singing named after their trade

explanation.surface: What tunes should be played at a dance for hairdressers?
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of close-harmony unaccompanied singing, named after men's hair salons.

clue.text: Mark has school backing

indicators.note: backing means the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Mark has the support of his school.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is a mark or sign, as in taking note or making a written mark.

clue.text: Stevedore who doesn't carry as much weight as others?

definitions.text: Stevedore who doesn't carry as much weight as others?

parts.words: Stevedore who doesn't carry as much weight as others?
parts.note: a dock worker who is a less heavy man; really one who works a barge used to load and unload ships

explanation.surface: A docker who carries less of the load than his colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: This worker operates a lighter, a flat barge carrying cargo to and from ships, akin to a docker.
